public_rationale: This is an open-ended forecast ('never') with no deadline. It could be settled early only by a decisive event: a general-purpose LLM shown in broad independent tests to work reliably, with near-zero hallucination and reasoning errors. No such event was found by October 2026. In September 2025, OpenAI said its newest model hallucinates less but still does, and that hallucinations remain a fundamental challenge for all LLMs. That fits Marcus's view so far but cannot confirm 'never'.
limitations: Searches for 2026 independent hallucination evaluations were limited.
What counts as 'reliable' and as an 'LLM' is open to interpretation.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: general-purpose LLMs (pure LLMs, not hybrid neurosymbolic systems) will never reach reliable performance across general tasks, meaning free of frequent hallucinations and reasoning errors, as many hoped in 2023.
'Never' has no deadline. The forecast can be contradicted early by a decisive event but cannot be confirmed by any finite date.
Whether reasoning models with tools still count as 'LLMs' is an open question in the claim itself.
criteria.support_condition: Cannot be finally confirmed at any finite date. Continued hallucination and error in leading LLMs is consistent with the claim but does not settle it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad independent evaluations show a general-purpose LLM working reliably across diverse real-world tasks, for example near-zero hallucination and reasoning-error rates comparable to dependable software.
